$comment: Coldline Task 3.11 public answer contract. Three run entries copied from the student's own latency harness output (one per provider: status, p50, p95, and the two error counts, or not_run with null figures for an Ollama run that could not happen), a structured primary and fallback decision, the condition that triggers the switch, and a bounded note. The provider contract checks compare each ran entry with its committed latency file as written and require primary to differ from fallback; the protected check compares primary, fallback, and fallback_trigger with the answer key. There is no self-attestation field, no pass boolean, and no endpoint URL.
title: Coldline Task 3.11 answers
description: The three provider runs, the primary and fallback decision, the fallback trigger, and the note.

answers.description: The only top-level answer mapping accepted by the public verifier.

runs.description: One entry per provider the harness can measure, keyed as the answer sheet names them.

primary.description: The provider the worker should call first for every summary.

fallback.description: The provider the worker should switch to when the primary fails the way fallback_trigger names; must differ from primary.

fallback_trigger.description: The observable condition under which the worker switches from the primary to the fallback.

notes.description: At most 600 characters: the provider on the fixture's first line, one limit of what your runs prove about each of the primary and the fallback, and whether a server built for serving open models would change the choice and why.

provider_choice.description: ollama (a self-hosted Ollama), hosted_api (the hosted provider the fixture was recorded from), or emulator (the deterministic local provider the worker calls today).

figure.description: A whole number copied from the harness output, or null when the run did not happen.

run.description: One provider's run: ran with the four figures copied from its latency file, or not_run with all four null.
